ours_text: A method is provided for generating an image from a medical device comprising an imaging system, an imaging device comprising a first and second section of the device, and an imaging device comprising a proximal portion of the device. In addition, the imaging device may be calibrated according to the orientation of the device. The imaging device comprises a plurality of instruments that are aligned at one end of the device with respect to a body surface, and a polarity modulator is applied to the instrument to determine the position of the instrument relative to the body surface.
baseline_run1: Systems and methods are disclosed for coordinated calibration and control of multiple medical instruments using multi-source imaging. A first interventional instrument is advanced to an anatomical site along a first trajectory, while one or more imaging instruments, each following distinct access paths, acquire image data of the site and the first instrument from multiple perspectives. A set of coordinate frames associated with the interventional instrument and the multiple imaging sources is registered, and differences between the frames are computed. A unified control reference frame is dynamically updated based at least in part on the computed differences and the multi-source image data to enhance guidance, navigation, and targeting accuracy during a medical procedure.
baseline_run2: Systems and methods are provided for multi-source image-guided calibration and control of medical instruments. A first instrument is configured to access an anatomical site via a first access path and to be controlled in a first control frame of reference, while a plurality of second instruments, each incorporating an imaging component, are configured to access the anatomical site via respective additional access paths and provide image data of the anatomical site and the first instrument. Differences between coordinate frames associated with each imaging source and the first instrument are determined and fused into a unified control frame of reference. The unified control frame is iteratively updated based on multi-source imaging data to enhance spatial accuracy, redundancy, and robustness of instrument guidance during medical procedures.
baseline_run3: Devices, systems, and methods are disclosed for multi-source image-guided calibration and control of medical instruments. A first instrument is configured to access an anatomical site along a first path and is controlled in a first coordinate frame, while one or more additional instruments, each along respective access paths, include imaging components that provide multi-source image data of the anatomical site and the first instrument. A processor is configured to jointly register the multi-source image data, determine differences between coordinate frames associated with the instruments, and update a control frame of reference for the first instrument based at least in part on the fused imaging information. The updated control frame facilitates enhanced navigation, targeting, and procedural accuracy using coordinated multi-source imaging.

ours_text: A surgical imaging system comprises a device that is actuated by a first and second axis to determine the position of an instrument relative to a focal point. The instrument is synchronized with a detector at one end of the device, and a detector at the other end of the device is synchronized with a detector at the other end of the device. A signal transmission method comprising an array of optically modulated light sources may be employed to control the output of an optically modulated light source from a detector at one end of the device.
baseline_run1: A system and method are provided for multi-path, coordinated medical imaging and instrument calibration using shared, multiplexed optical resources. A first medical instrument accesses an anatomical site via a first path and is controlled in a first coordinate frame, while one or more second instruments with imaging components access the site via different paths and operate in corresponding coordinate frames. A multiplexed imaging architecture employs multiple scanning devices and light receivers with waveband separation, temporal multiplexing, and/or modulation-demodulation schemes to generate co-registered images from the plurality of access paths while avoiding crosstalk. Differences between the coordinate frames are computed based on the multiplexed imaging data, and a control frame of reference associated with the first instrument is dynamically updated to provide accurate guidance and calibration across the multiple instrument access paths.
baseline_run2: A system and method are provided for multi-path, multi-device image-guided calibration of medical instruments accessing a common anatomical site. A plurality of scanning instruments, each following a distinct access path, are configured with imaging components that operate using temporally or spectrally multiplexed light to avoid crosstalk and to share common light sources, detectors, and processing resources. Image data from the plurality of instruments are used to determine differences between respective instrument coordinate frames and a unified control frame of reference for an actively controlled or navigated instrument. The unified control frame is iteratively updated based at least in part on the demodulated, device-specific image signals to enhance registration accuracy and coordinated guidance of the instruments within the anatomical site.
baseline_run3: A system and method are provided for multi-instrument medical navigation and imaging using shared, multiplexed optical resources. A first medical instrument accesses an anatomical site along a first path and is controlled in a first coordinate frame, while one or more second instruments, each equipped with an imaging or scanning component, access the site along different paths and operate in respective second coordinate frames. A plurality of scanning devices and light receivers are driven using shared light sources, detectors, and controllers, with crosstalk between instruments mitigated via wavelength division, temporal multiplexing, or modulation/demodulation schemes so that image data from each instrument is separable. A control frame of reference associated with the first instrument is dynamically updated based at least in part on differences between instrument coordinate frames derived from the multiplexed image data, thereby providing coordinated, low-cost, multi-instrument guidance.

ours_text: A system of the present invention provides a method for controlling and manipulating a surgical device. The system includes a motion sensor and a control mechanism for detecting and manipulating the motion of a surgical device. The control mechanism emits a resonant energy generated by the first and second components of the control mechanism. The resonant energy generated by the first and second components of the control mechanism is transmitted to a user at a fixed location. The resonant energy generated by the third component is transmitted to a user at a fixed location to be viewed.
baseline_run1: A system and method are provided for robotically assisted surgical removal of hard or non-fibrous tissue using multi-axis robotic instruments with coordinated calibration. A first robotic instrument comprising a reciprocating tool is configured to access an anatomical site along a first access path for tissue removal, while a second robotic instrument comprising an imaging component is configured to access the anatomical site along a second access path to obtain real-time image data of the anatomical site and the first instrument. A control unit determines a difference between a first coordinate frame associated with the tissue-removal instrument and a second coordinate frame associated with the imaging instrument. Based at least in part on the determined difference, the system updates a control frame of reference for the tissue-removal instrument to enable precise, image-guided robotic resection while preserving surrounding soft tissue.
baseline_run2: A system and method are provided for robotically assisted surgical bone removal with dynamic instrument calibration using intraoperative imaging. A first robotically controlled bone-removal instrument accesses a target anatomical site along a first access path, while a second instrument with an imaging component accesses the site along a second access path and generates real-time image data of the anatomy and the first instrument. A control system determines a difference between a coordinate frame of the first instrument and a coordinate frame of the imaging instrument, and updates a control frame of reference for the robotic bone-removal tool based on the difference. The updated control frame enables precise, image-guided robotic resection of hard tissue while maintaining safe separation from adjacent soft tissues, and may be operated locally or via telemanipulation.
baseline_run3: A system and method are provided for robotically assisted surgical procedures that employ coordinated calibration between multiple instruments accessing a common anatomical site. A first robotically controlled instrument including a reciprocating tool is configured to remove hard or non-fibrous tissues along a planned trajectory, while a second instrument including an imaging component accesses the anatomical site along a different path to acquire real-time image data of the site and the first instrument. A difference between a coordinate frame associated with the first instrument and a coordinate frame associated with the second instrument is determined based at least in part on the acquired image data. A control frame of reference of the robotically controlled instrument is updated in response to the determined difference to enhance accuracy, safety, and remote operability of the tissue-removal procedure.

ours_text: A surgical instrument system comprises a robotically actuated endoscope capable of manipulating a portion of a patient's body cavity. The robotically actuated endoscope is positioned proximal to the surgical instrument, and a guiding device is positioned proximal to the surgical instrument. The method of the invention includes a first-line technique for removing a portion of a patient's body cavity from a surgical instrument, and a second-line technique for insertion of a surgical instrument through a longitudinal slit.
baseline_run1: A system and method are provided for coordinated robotic endoscopic-percutaneous surgical procedures. The system includes a surgical platform carrying a first robotic arm that manipulably controls a percutaneous instrument and a second robotic arm that manipulably controls an endoscopic instrument inserted through a natural orifice, each arm having position sensing capability. A control circuit determines and registers the positions of both instruments within a common anatomical coordinate frame, defines a target location within a treatment region based on endoscopic sensing, and automatically guides the percutaneous instrument toward the target location while compensating for changes in platform position. The control circuit further coordinates cooperative interaction between the percutaneous and endoscopic instruments to perform diagnostic and therapeutic tasks within the treatment region.
baseline_run2: A robotic surgical system enables coordinated endoscopic and percutaneous interventions within a patient using a common surgical platform. A first robotic arm manipulates an endoscopic instrument with an onboard position sensor introduced through a natural orifice to map and define a target location within a treatment region. A second robotic arm percutaneously guides a therapeutic instrument toward the defined target location, with the control circuit compensating for patient and platform motion and dynamically adjusting both arms’ positions and orientations. The control circuit further coordinates cooperative interaction between the endoscopic and percutaneous instruments to perform image-guided, robotically assisted surgical procedures at or near the target location.
baseline_run3: A prospective system enables coordinated endoscopic and percutaneous robotic interventions using shared spatial registration and cooperative control. An elongated endoscopic instrument with an onboard position sensor is passed through a natural orifice to a treatment region, where its position is tracked and used to define one or more internal target locations. A surgical platform supporting multiple robotic arms then percutaneously guides secondary instruments toward the defined targets, automatically compensating for platform motion and patient movement. A control circuit synchronizes the positions and orientations of the endoscopic and percutaneous instruments to cooperatively perform complex procedures such as triangulation, tissue manipulation, and targeted therapy delivery.

ours_text: 1 A method for manipulating surgical instruments comprises a catheter-shaped endoscope and a catheter-shaped guide device. The catheter-shaped guide device generates an image of the catheter-shaped guide device. The catheter-shaped guide device generates an image of the catheter-shaped guide device. In addition, the method is able to determine a relative position of the catheter-shaped guide device within a patient's body cavity without the need for a radial emission system. In addition, the method is able to identify a point of obstruction within a patient's body cavity.
baseline_run1: A system and method are provided for robotically assisted, endoscopically guided percutaneous interventions using multi-sensor electromagnetic tracking. A first medical instrument including an elongated shaft and a plurality of distal electromagnetic sensors is introduced through a natural orifice, its six-degree-of-freedom pose continuously determined relative to an external field generator array to define a dynamic treatment map. A target location within the treatment region is identified based on the tracked pose of the first instrument, and a second medical instrument is percutaneously advanced under robotic control and real-time electromagnetic localization toward the target. The system integrates sensor fusion between endoscopic and percutaneous instruments to improve registration accuracy, procedural guidance, and safety in minimally invasive therapies.
baseline_run2: Systems and methods are provided for robotically assisted, endoscopically guided percutaneous interventions using multi-sensor electromagnetic localization. An endoscopic instrument having an elongated shaft and a plurality of distal magnetic field sensors is inserted through a natural orifice into a treatment region, and its three-dimensional position and orientation are determined relative to an external reference frame using distinguishable AC magnetic fields generated by multiple field generators. A target location within the treatment region is defined based on the localized endoscope, and a percutaneous instrument under robotic control is guided toward the target using the same electromagnetic locating system for continuous tracking and alignment. The integrated system enables coordinated navigation, real-time targeting, and precise tool-to-target registration for minimally invasive procedures.
baseline_run3: Systems and methods are disclosed for robotically-assisted percutaneous interventions that integrate multi-sensor magnetic tracking with endoscopic navigation. An endoscope carrying a plurality of magnetic field sensors is advanced through a natural orifice into a treatment region, where its six-degree-of-freedom pose is determined relative to external field generators. A robotic controller defines a target location within the treatment region based on the tracked endoscope position and subsequently guides a percutaneously introduced instrument toward the target under real-time positional feedback. The system thereby coordinates internal endoscopic visualization and tracking with external percutaneous tool navigation to improve accuracy and safety of minimally invasive procedures.

ours_text: A surgical tool system comprises a surgical instrument capable of manipulating an endoscope to perform a surgical procedure at a location proximal to the endoscope. A surgical instrument comprises a first-axis rotational motor coupled to a cutting tool. A surgical instrument comprises a laser-guided image transmission device. The laser-guided image transmission device is coupled to a cutting tool. A method for determining the position of a surgical instrument is also provided, and a method for determining the position of a surgical instrument is also provided, and a method for.
baseline_run1: Systems and methods are provided for lifecycle-aware, robotically-assisted endoscopic-percutaneous procedures. A first instrument having an elongated shaft, a position sensor, and at least one usage sensor is inserted endoscopically into a treatment region, its position determined, and a target location defined. A second percutaneous robotic instrument is guided toward the target location while images captured during the procedure are used to identify instrument types and correlate them with sensor-derived usage data. Based on the identified instrument type and aggregated usage data across procedures, a stage in each instrument’s life cycle is determined and used to control instrument selection, provide maintenance alerts, and adjust procedural planning in real time.
baseline_run2: A system and method for managing robotically-assisted endoscopic-percutaneous procedures integrates real-time instrument tracking with lifecycle monitoring. A first endoscopic instrument including a position sensor is inserted through a natural orifice to define a target location within a treatment region, while a second robotic instrument is percutaneously guided toward the target location. One or more imagers capture images of the instruments during the procedure, and a processor identifies instrument type and determines a degree of usage based on sensor data and image-derived information. The system further determines a lifecycle stage of each instrument and generates guidance or alerts regarding instrument deployment, replacement, or reuse during or after the robotically-enabled procedure.
baseline_run3: A system for managing endoscopically-assisted percutaneous robotic procedures includes a first instrument having an elongated shaft, a position sensor, and a usage-tracking module, and a second percutaneously-introduced robotic instrument. The system determines a three-dimensional position of the first instrument within a treatment region via the position sensor and defines a target location for percutaneous approach. An imager captures images of the first and second instruments during the procedure, and a processor identifies instrument types and determines degrees of usage from sensor data to track life-cycle stages of each instrument. The robotic system uses both positional and life-cycle information to guide the second instrument toward the target location while enforcing instrument usage limits and replacement scheduling.

ours_text: A system comprises a device for manipulating and tagging surgical instruments. The system includes a method for determining the position of a surgical instrument at a particular location. The method includes a first-arm motion detector coupled to one of the first-arm motion detectors. The method includes a set of control circuits that are electrically connected to at least one end of the system. In addition, a plurality of data input and output channels are provided to the system for generating and tagging a biometric image of the system.
baseline_run1: Systems and methods are provided for coordinated robotic medical procedures that integrate fiducial-based identification and tracking with multi-port robotic tool control. A robotic camera and multiple robotic instruments are inserted through separate patient ports, wherein fiducial markers disposed on tissue, instruments, or port structures are automatically detected and tracked in real time. The system dynamically adjusts remote centers of motion and coordinated tool trajectories based on fiducial-derived pose information to maintain instruments within the camera’s field of view and relative to targeted anatomical sites. Multiple control modes enable selective manual control of a camera or instrument while automatically updating the positions of other tools in response to changes in fiducial locations and orientations.
baseline_run2: Disclosed are robotic medical systems and methods that integrate coordinated multi-tool control with automated fiducial-based tracking to enhance intraoperative guidance. A robotic camera and multiple robotic tools inserted through separate ports are controlled in coordinated motion while maintaining remote centers of motion, with the positions and orientations of the tools and anatomical targets continuously updated using fiducial identification and tracking. In various modes, the camera and tools are automatically repositioned to maintain all relevant fiducials within the field of view and to align tool trajectories with fiducial-defined target regions. The system thereby enables dynamic, image-guided, and cooperative manipulation of multiple instruments with improved accuracy and situational awareness.
baseline_run3: Systems and methods are provided for robotically assisted medical procedures that integrate coordinated multi-tool control with fiducial-based identification and tracking. A robotic medical system includes a camera and multiple robotic tools inserted through separate ports, wherein movements of the tools and camera are automatically coordinated while maintaining remote centers of motion and ensuring that the tools remain within the camera’s field of view. Fiducial markers disposed on tools, instruments, anatomical landmarks, or implants are automatically identified and tracked in real time, and their positions are used to refine tool trajectories, update virtual overlays, and enhance coordination of camera and tool motion. The system may operate in multiple control modes in which user input on one or more controllers is combined with fiducial tracking data to dynamically adjust coordinated movements and improve procedural accuracy and safety.

ours_text: A medical robotic device of the invention comprises a coupling system to provide a method for manipulating a body cavity during a surgical procedure. The device is positioned within the body cavity to provide a recognizable image to the user. The device is positioned in the body cavity to provide a recognizable image to the user. The invention also provides a method for inserting an endoscope into a patient, wherein the endoscope is operated on by a centrally operated device, wherein the endoscope is operated on by a centrally controlled device.
baseline_run1: A robotic image-guided interventional system and methods are provided for coordinating multiple intracavitary robotic tools and needle-based instruments under real-time medical imaging. A multi-port robotic platform with remote centers of motion positions and orients a camera and one or more therapeutic or diagnostic tools within a body cavity, while a three degree-of-freedom intracavitary mechanism advances and steers a needle toward an image-selected target. In response to user inputs at one or more controllers, networked computers process imaging data to automatically adjust the coordinated motion of the camera, tools, and needle so that the working instruments remain within the field of view and follow an optimized image-guided trajectory. The system enables remote or local operation inside MRI, CT, ultrasound, or X-ray environments while maintaining precise, coordinated alignment among visualization, access, and needle insertion paths.
baseline_run2: A robotic image-guided interventional system and methods are provided for performing coordinated multi-port procedures inside and adjacent to body cavities under real-time medical imaging. A plurality of robotic tools, including at least one steerable needle device adapted for operation within an MRI, CT, fluoroscopy, or ultrasound imager, are inserted through separate ports or natural orifices and are controlled to maintain remote centers of motion while executing coordinated movements. A robotic camera or imaging-localized end effector is controlled in a first mode to define a dynamic field of interest, with the steerable needle and additional tools automatically coordinated to remain within this field and follow image-defined trajectories to target locations. In a second mode, a master controller directs the steerable needle device and associated tools toward image-selected targets while the camera or imaging reference automatically repositions to maintain optimal visualization and imaging compatibility.
baseline_run3: A robotic image-guided interventional system and related methods are provided for performing coordinated, minimally invasive procedures within a patient using multiple robotic tools deployed through body cavities or laparoscopic ports under real-time medical imaging. A first controller actuates a 3-degree-of-freedom mechanical device configured to translate and rotate within a cavity and to advance and steer a needle toward a user-selected target within the imaging volume, while additional robotic tools and a robotic camera are automatically moved in coordinated fashion to maintain remote centers of motion and preserve a desired field of view. A second controller enables independent or shared control of the robotic camera, with automatic adjustment of the needle-guidance device and ancillary tools to remain within the imaging plane and camera view. Networked computers process real-time images from MRI, CT, fluoroscopy, or ultrasound, compute coordinated motion commands, and provide closed-loop control of the multi-tool robotic system for precise, image-guided targeting and intervention.

ours_text: A system of the invention includes a method for manipulating a surgical instrument, a device comprising at least one robotic actuator coupled to said actuator, and a device comprising a first-order camera coupled to said actuator. A method for obtaining and analyzing a patient's body position relative to said surgical instrument is provided. A method for transmitting and analyzing a patient's body position relative to said surgical instrument is provided. One or more embodiments of said embodiments may be configured to provide an electrical power source within said device.
baseline_run1: Disclosed are systems and methods for context-aware coordinated control of multiple robotic medical tools and imaging devices during a medical procedure. A robotic controller maintains remote centers of motion while automatically coordinating the movements of multiple tools and at least one robotic camera, and dynamically adjusts their relative positions to preserve tool visibility within the camera’s field of view. Configuration parameters and control modes for the tools and imaging devices are adaptively selected based on real-time detection of instruments, procedure phase, and image-based contextual measures. In some embodiments, the inferred procedural context is further used to switch between different imaging modalities and to autonomously reorient tools and cameras for optimized access, safety, and visualization.
baseline_run2: Systems and methods are provided for context-aware coordinated control of multiple robotic medical tools and imaging devices during a medical procedure. A robotic medical system maintains remote centers of motion while coordinating movements of therapeutic tools and robotic cameras, and dynamically reconfigures control modes based on the detected phase, context, or state of the procedure. Image-based identification of instruments and real-time inference of procedural phase are used to automatically adjust tool trajectories, camera viewpoints, and control assignments between operators and autonomous modes. In some embodiments, detection of specific tools or procedural contexts triggers adaptive switching between imaging modalities and corresponding updates to coordinated motion strategies.
baseline_run3: A robotic medical system is provided that adaptively coordinates multiple robotic tools and imaging devices during a medical procedure based on real-time procedural context. A controller maintains remote centers of motion while automatically adjusting the positions and orientations of robotic instruments and cameras in coordinated movements responsive to detected instruments, surgical phase, or region of interest. Image-based detection and instrument identification are used to infer the current state or phase of the procedure and to dynamically reconfigure control modes, such as prioritizing field-of-view maintenance, instrument-centric coordination, or modality switching between imaging systems. The system thereby optimizes tool positioning, visualization, and device configurations throughout the evolving course of the procedure.

ours_text: A method for actuating a surgical manipulating device includes a virtual user interface and a computer-based control system. The virtual user interface provides haptic feedback to a surgical manipulating device. The virtual user interface provides a method for actuating a surgical manipulating device at a predetermined position relative to a haptic force source. The device may be equipped with a receptacle to store a haptic force source, which is used to determine the shape of a surgical instrument. The device may be equipped with a three-dimensional shape.
baseline_run1: A remotely operated surgical actuator system includes an elongated guide section with a distal end member carrying a surgical tool, and a drive source for changing the attitude of the distal end member via an internal attitude operation member. A non-contact attitude detection device detects the orientation of the distal end member relative to the guide section, and correction means adjust command values supplied to the drive source to compensate for product-to-product variations in distal end straightness. A processing circuit associates the surgical tool with a virtual haptic interaction point, establishes at least one virtual entry boundary within a surgical workspace, and activates a haptic object that constrains movement of the tool when the virtual haptic interaction point crosses the boundary. The correction and haptic constraint control operate cooperatively to provide accurate, stable, and safe tool positioning during remote surgical procedures.
baseline_run2: A remotely operated surgical actuator system includes an elongated guide section with a distal end member supporting a surgical tool, and a control unit configured to change the attitude of the distal end member via an internally disposed attitude operation member. A non-contact attitude detection device detects the orientation of the distal end member relative to the guide section, and a correction means adjusts command values to a drive source based on the detected attitude to compensate for product variation and bending. A processing circuit associates the surgical tool with a virtual haptic interaction point and defines a virtual entry boundary within a surgical workspace. When the virtual haptic interaction point crosses the virtual entry boundary, a haptic object is activated to constrain movement of the surgical tool in accordance with the corrected attitude control, thereby improving precision and safety of remote surgical manipulation.
baseline_run3: A surgical manipulation system comprises an elongated guide section having a distal end member that supports a surgical tool, and a drive source configured to advance and retract an attitude operation member within the guide section to change the attitude of the distal end member. An attitude detection device non‑contactingly detects the attitude of the distal end member relative to the guide section, and a control unit corrects command values to the drive source based on the detected attitude. A virtual haptic interaction point is associated with the surgical tool such that movement of the virtual haptic interaction point corresponds to movement and attitude of the distal end member. The control unit further establishes a virtual entry boundary and activates a haptic object that constrains motion of the distal end member and surgical tool after the virtual haptic interaction point crosses the virtual entry boundary, thereby providing corrected, haptically guided attitude control during surgery.

ours_text: One of the methods of the present invention includes a virtual surgical tool system for manipulating anatomical data generated by a computer and displaying it to a user during a surgical procedure. The system is configured to detect anatomical changes in a patient during a surgical procedure. A user interface is configured to provide feedback to a surgeon on the anatomical position of a surgical implant. The anatomical position of a surgical implant can be correlated with the anatomical position of a surgical instrument, based on a combination of physical and electro-mechanical parameters.
baseline_run1: A surgical system and method are disclosed for performing computer-assisted surgery using patient-specific anatomy models combined with haptic-constrained tool guidance. A three-dimensional model of the patient’s anatomy is generated, and an optimal implant orientation and position are determined to design patient-matched instrumentation that defines virtual entry boundaries and safe tool paths. A surgical tool, associated with a virtual haptic interaction point, is registered to the patient-matched instrumentation, and a processing circuit activates haptic objects that constrain tool motion when the virtual haptic interaction point approaches or crosses the predefined boundaries. The system thereby provides real-time, anatomy-specific haptic feedback to guide the surgeon along planned trajectories while preventing deviation outside the virtual constraints.
baseline_run2: A surgical system and method are disclosed for performing computer-assisted procedures using patient-specific 3D anatomical models in combination with virtual haptic guidance. A 3D model of the patient’s affected area is generated, and patient-matched instrumentation is created and positioned on the anatomy to acquire registration information and define an implant orientation and position. A surgical tool, registered to the model and associated with a virtual haptic interaction point, is then constrained by one or more virtual entry boundaries and haptic objects that correspond to planned surgical paths and implant locations. Movement of the tool is thus haptically guided within the patient-specific virtual environment to improve accuracy and safety of the surgical procedure.
baseline_run3: A surgical system and method are disclosed that integrate patient-specific 3D anatomical modeling and virtual haptic boundary control for computer-assisted surgery. A 3D model of the patient’s affected area is generated and used to determine an implant orientation and position, and to design patient-matched instrumentation that serves as a physical registration interface for a computer-assisted surgical tool. A virtual haptic interaction point associated with the surgical tool is registered to the patient’s anatomy via the patient-matched instrumentation, enabling establishment of virtual entry boundaries and haptic objects that constrain tool motion relative to the planned implant position. The system thereby provides guided, constrained tool manipulation within the patient-specific anatomy to enhance accuracy and safety of implant placement.

ours_text: A bi-sectional endoscopy device of the present invention comprises an implantable catheter that is able to be inserted into a body cavity for the purpose of generating an image of the surrounding tissue. The implantable catheter is anchored to the endoscope by means of a flexible suture. In addition, the implantable catheter is equipped with a magnetically activated ligand, a receptacle, and a protruding membrane. The ligand is positioned at the surface of the implantable catheter to facilitate insertion and dissection.
baseline_run1: A surgical system for image-guided, magnetically assisted anastomosis combines an endoscopic-ultrasound image fusion workstation with an implantable magnetic anastomosis device. The system includes an image fusion controller configured to detect a laparoscopic ultrasound probe and a delivery endoscope within a common field-of-view and to generate a fused endoscopic-ultrasound image of a target anatomical region. Based on the fused image space, a navigation module guides minimally-invasive deployment and self-assembly of a linear-configured magnetic exoskeleton device into a polygonal configuration circumscribing tissue selected for anastomosis. The fused imaging further enables real-time assessment of device placement, tissue apposition, and subsequent formation of the anastomosis.
baseline_run2: A system and method for image-guided deployment of an implantable magnetic anastomosis device using fused endoscopic and laparoscopic ultrasound imaging is disclosed. An image fusion workstation registers an endoscopic image space to an ultrasound image space by detecting an ultrasound probe within the endoscope field-of-view, and generates a real-time fused visualization of the target tissue region. The magnetic anastomosis device, deliverable in a linear configuration via the endoscope or laparoscopic port, is navigated and positioned under this fused guidance to self-assemble into a predefined polygonal configuration circumscribing the selected tissue. The fused imaging enables precise placement, monitoring of tissue apposition, and verification of anastomosis formation and patency over time.
baseline_run3: A system and method for image-guided deployment of an implantable magnetic anastomosis device using fused intraoperative imaging is disclosed. An image fusion workstation registers and fuses a real-time endoscopic or laparoscopic image of an anatomical region with an ultrasound image acquired by a laparoscopic ultrasound probe, based on detection and tracking of the probe within the endoscopic field of view. The fused image stream is used to plan, guide, and verify minimally-invasive delivery and self-assembly of a magnetic anastomosis device from a linear to a polygonal configuration around a selected tissue segment. The system further enables real-time assessment of tissue apposition, perfusion, and eventual necrosis/perforation at the anastomosis site, thereby improving precision and safety of magnetic anastomosis procedures.

ours_text: An endoscopic surgical tool comprises a robot-operated manipulator arm with a coupling mechanism that allows the manipulator arm to move relative to a surgical instrument. The coupling mechanism allows the manipulator arm to be flexibly accessed by a surgical instrument. A drive shaft is attached to the manipulator arm. The assembly includes a handle for controlling the movement of a surgical instrument, and a first-in, first-out, and second-in, middle-in, and third-in device for removing tissue from a surgical instrument.
baseline_run1: A robotic surgical system includes a control system operatively coupled to one or more minimally invasive robotic instruments each having an end effector driven through a compact U-turn actuation mechanism. The U-turn mechanism transmits actuating forces around a tight bend radius between proximal drive elements and a distal wrist and end effector, enabling articulation within constrained anatomical spaces. One or more sensors disposed along the instrument and within the U-turn mechanism measure forces, torques, and velocities associated with the distal components. The control system processes the sensed data to determine movement parameters and actively modulate actuation through the U-turn mechanism, thereby providing precise control of tissue manipulation and cutting while mitigating unintended tissue damage.
baseline_run2: A robotic minimally invasive surgical system is disclosed in which a control system manipulates one or more robotic arms coupled to elongated tool assemblies incorporating compact U-turn mechanisms. Each tool assembly includes an end effector and optionally a wrist mechanism positioned distal to a U-turn mechanism that transmits actuating forces around a tight bend radius, enabling complex distal articulation within confined anatomical spaces. One or more sensors disposed along the shaft and near the U-turn mechanism measure forces, velocities, and tensions associated with the robotic arm and distal components. The control system processes the sensed data to determine movement parameters that coordinate robotic arm motion with U-turn force transmission, thereby precisely controlling tissue cutting or manipulation while reducing the risk of unintended tissue damage.
baseline_run3: A robotic surgical system comprises a control system operatively coupled to at least one robotic arm supporting a minimally invasive instrument having a U-turn mechanism for transmitting actuating forces around a compact bend. The U-turn mechanism is configured to route control forces to a distal wrist and end effector through a bend radius smaller than that of comparable flexible arms while maintaining precise motion transmission. One or more sensors are disposed along the instrument and at the end effector to measure forces, velocities, or tensions associated with tissue interaction and instrument motion. The control system processes the sensed data to determine and adjust movement parameters of the robotic arm and U-turn-actuated distal components to achieve controlled tissue manipulation and cutting while reducing unintended tissue damage.

ours_text: A method for a patient undergoing orthopaedic surgery comprises a device for positioning and adjusting the anatomical portion of a bone implant in a joint. The device may be augmented with a computer-generated guidance system to generate a map of the anatomical portion of a bone implant. In addition, the invention includes methods for obtaining data from a multi-probe imaging system, such as a digital camera, which is used to identify the location of the implant in relation to the anatomical portion of the joint.
baseline_run1: A system and method are provided for navigated orthopedic revision surgery utilizing a hand-held imaging device and existing implants as registration references. The system includes a radiation-based hand-held imaging unit with an integrated detector and a navigation system configured to track the pose of the imaging unit in real time relative to the patient. Image data acquired from the tracked device is registered to the known geometry and spatial position of an in-situ orthopedic implant, allowing precise localization and guided removal of bone, bone cement, and/or the prosthesis. The system may further interface with robotic or articulating hand-held tools to execute computer-assisted, image-guided resection and implant extraction with improved accuracy and reduced invasiveness.
baseline_run2: A system and method are provided for computer-assisted revision orthopedic surgery that integrates intraoperative imaging with implant-based registration. A hand-held radiation imaging device with a tracked pose acquires real-time image data of a previously implanted prosthesis and surrounding bone and/or bone cement. The navigation system uses the known geometry and position of the existing implant, as visualized in the tracked images, to automatically register the patient anatomy and guide precise removal of bone, cement, and/or the prosthesis. The system may be used with robotic or articulating hand-held tools to execute planned cuts or removal paths based on the intraoperative imaging and implant-based registration.
baseline_run3: A system and method are provided for navigated orthopedic revision surgery that integrates a hand-held imaging device with an existing implanted prosthesis as a registration landmark. The system includes a radiation-based hand-held imaging probe tracked by a navigation system to acquire intraoperative images of bone, bone cement, and prosthetic interfaces, and to determine the pose of the device relative to the implant. Using the known geometry and spatial position of the existing implant, the system generates a real-time, registered anatomical model that guides removal of bone, bone cement, and/or the prosthesis. The system may further interface with robotic or articulating hand-held cutting tools to execute planned removal trajectories with enhanced accuracy and reduced damage to surrounding tissue.

ours_text: 1 The invention comprises a method for establishing a bone satchet relative to the surface of the body of the first osteotomy. The technique is achieved by cutting a portion of a bone satchet into the surface of the body of the first osteotomy. The insertion point of the insertion point is controlled by a coupling tool, which provides a positional adjustment of the insertion point relative to the surface of the body of the first osteotomy. The coupling tool provides a positional adjustment of the insertion point relative to the surface.
baseline_run1: A system and method for computer-assisted wedge-opening osteotomy is provided, comprising a bone fixation plate and a haptic-enabled virtual planning environment. The system includes a computer configured to generate a patient-specific bone model, simulate formation of first and second bone voids and corresponding cut surfaces, and virtually position a fixation plate having first and second holes. The computer is further configured to compute haptic interaction geometric primitives corresponding to plate-bone alignment and osteotomy gap manipulation, and to determine haptic forces in distinct subspaces corresponding to translational and rotational adjustments of the bone segments. A haptic interface outputs substantially stable haptic feedback to guide the surgeon in achieving desired alignment before physical cutting and fixation with fasteners.
baseline_run2: A surgical guidance system for wedge-opening osteotomy integrates virtual haptic interaction with bone fixation planning. A computer generates a virtual model of a bone, a fixation plate having first and second holes, and associated fasteners, and defines haptic interaction geometric primitives corresponding to cutting planes and planned fastener void locations. The computer determines, in a first haptic subspace, forces that guide a virtual or robot-assisted tool along predetermined osteotomy cut paths and void-formation trajectories, and in a second, different haptic subspace, forces that guide alignment of the plate holes with the formed bone voids as the cut bone segments are repositioned. The system provides substantially stable haptic feedback to the surgeon or robotic instrument during cutting, repositioning, and plate fixation to improve accuracy of osteotomy gap opening and hardware placement.
baseline_run3: A computer-assisted orthopedic osteotomy system is provided that combines a fixation plate and guided cutting methodology with real-time haptic feedback in multiple subspaces. The system includes a bone fixation plate having first and second apertures configured to define corresponding bone voids used as cutting and repositioning references, and a virtual surgical tool rendered in a mixed-reality or robotic interface. A processor identifies first and second subsets of haptic interaction geometric primitives corresponding respectively to an approach/cutting subspace and a repositioning/fixation subspace, and computes haptic forces for each subspace to guide the surgeon’s tool path and bone-segment manipulation. By aligning the fixation plate apertures with the bone voids while providing substantially stable multi-subspace haptic feedback, the system enhances accuracy and stability of wedge-opening osteotomy planning, execution, and fixation.

ours_text: An imaging system includes a radiation source formed to capture a photon of a radiation source, a handheld device disposed on a fixed surface, and a method of adjusting the position of the handheld device, a handheld device disposed on a fixed surface, and a navigation device disposed on the handheld device.
baseline_run1: A system and method for performing revision surgery integrates a hand-held imaging device with a robotic-assisted surgical system to facilitate implant removal. The hand-held imaging device includes a radiation source, detector, and navigation system configured to track its pose and acquire intraoperative image data of an implant-bone interface. The system processes the acquired image data to determine information related to the interface area and to generate a planned virtual boundary for removal of a portion of the interface. A robotic system tracks a cutting tool in physical space, correlates its movement with a virtual tool, and constrains the cutting tool based on the planned virtual boundary to guide removal of the implant component from the bone.
baseline_run2: A system and method for robot-assisted revision surgery utilizes a hand-held, tracked imaging device to acquire intraoperative image data of an implant-bone interface. The navigation system determines the pose of the hand-held imaging device and generates an updated three-dimensional representation of the implant and surrounding bone. Based on this representation, the system determines interface information and computes a planned virtual boundary for material removal to facilitate implant extraction. A robotic cutting tool is then tracked and constrained relative to the planned virtual boundary, such that cutting is dynamically guided and limited according to the real-time imaging and pose-tracked updates.
baseline_run3: A system and method for performing revision surgery combines a robotic-assisted surgery platform with a hand-held imaging and navigation device. The method includes using the hand-held imaging device having a radiation source and fixed detector, tracked in real time by a navigation system, to acquire intraoperative image data of an implant-bone interface region. Based on the acquired image data, the system determines information related to the interface area and generates a planned virtual boundary defining a portion of the interface to be removed. A robotic or navigated cutting tool is then tracked and constrained according to the planned virtual boundary, enabling guided removal of the implant component from the bone with updated intraoperative imaging feedback.

ours_text: 1 An orthopaedic surgery device comprising a base unit is configured to generate an image of a patient's position relative to a target joint. The device comprises a control mechanism for adjusting the position of a target joint. The device comprises a control mechanism for adjusting the position of a target joint relative to a target joint. In addition, the invention permits the use of a plurality of optical probes, including a hand-held device and a computer-aided image processing system.
baseline_run1: A system and method are disclosed for image-guided joint repair and implant revision that integrates a patient-specific joint reconstruction platform with a hand-held tracked imaging device. The system includes customized or highly selectable surgical tools and implant components adapted to an individual patient, and a radiation-based imaging device having a source and detector rigidly fixed together and tracked in real time by a navigation system. Intraoperative image data acquired by the hand-held imaging device are used to determine the pose of existing or damaged implants and surrounding anatomy, and to guide preparation of bone surfaces and placement of customized replacement components. The integration of customizable tools and real-time navigated imaging improves accuracy, speed, and adaptability during complete or partial joint arthroplasty and revision procedures.
baseline_run2: A system and method are disclosed for patient-specific joint repair using a tracked hand-held imaging device. The system comprises customized or highly selectable surgical tools and implant components configured for optimal fit and function in joint revision or replacement procedures, and a navigation-enabled imaging device having an integrated radiation source and detector to intraoperatively acquire three-dimensional image data of the joint region. The navigation system tracks the pose of the hand-held imaging device relative to the patient and surgical tools to provide real-time guidance for preparation of bone surfaces and placement of customized implants. The imaging and navigation data are further used to update and refine preoperative plans and to verify final implant position and joint function during the procedure.
baseline_run3: A system and method are disclosed for image-guided revision arthroplasty using a patient-specific, handheld imaging and navigation platform. The system comprises a handheld radiation-based imaging device having an integrated detector and pose-tracked by a navigation system, configured to acquire intraoperative images of a joint having a damaged implant. Patient-specific or highly selectable surgical tools and implant components are generated or selected based on preoperative and intraoperative imaging data, and their positioning is dynamically guided using the tracked handheld imager to optimize fit and function. The system improves speed, accuracy, and ease of performing complete or partial joint replacement or re-replacement procedures.

ours_text: A method of the invention relates to a computer-controlled system for generating a virtual haptic representation of a surgical procedure by using a combination of a simulated haptic model and a predetermined haptic model. The predetermined haptic model is then analyzed for morphological features, such as bone structure and joint surface area. Two methods of the invention are described for generating a virtual haptic representation of a surgical procedure by using a predetermined haptic model and adjusting a predetermined haptic model to a target.
baseline_run1: A system and method are disclosed for image-free, haptically guided orthopedic implant revision surgery. The method includes generating an initial 3D model of a target bone based on predefined anatomical parameters, collecting intraoperative surface points from exposed bone regions, and producing an updated, reshaped 3D bone model in real time. A haptic interface is configured with geometric interaction primitives associated with the reshaped 3D model, and the system identifies first and second subsets of the primitives to compute haptic forces in corresponding, different subspaces. The resulting haptic feedback provides substantially stable, spatially differentiated guidance to a virtual surgical tool, enabling accurate bone preparation and implant positioning without preoperative imaging.
baseline_run2: Systems and methods are disclosed for image-free computer-assisted orthopedic revision surgery with subspace-decomposed haptic guidance. A 3D model of a target bone and existing implant is generated from predefined anatomical parameters and intraoperatively acquired surface points, and is iteratively reshaped to reflect actual patient anatomy. A virtual surgical tool is defined in the modeled environment, and a haptic interaction engine identifies distinct subsets of geometric primitives associated with implant removal, bone preservation, and implant preparation. Haptic forces are computed in corresponding subspaces to provide substantially stable, task-specific tactile feedback that guides the surgeon in executing the revision plan while minimizing unintended bone removal.
baseline_run3: A system and method are provided for planning and executing image-free revision implant surgery with stable, multi-subspace haptic guidance. The system generates an initial three-dimensional model of a target bone using pre-defined anatomical parameters, acquires intraoperative surface points from the exposed bone, and produces a reshaped three-dimensional model reflecting the actual patient anatomy. A virtual surgical tool is associated with haptic interaction geometric primitives derived from the reshaped model, and a computer identifies distinct subsets of these primitives to define multiple haptic subspaces corresponding to different surgical tasks or regions. Haptic forces are computed separately in each subspace and combined to provide substantially stable, task-specific tactile feedback to guide bone preparation and implant placement during revision surgery without reliance on preoperative imaging.

ours_text: A method for generating and adjusting a computer-based haptic simulation of a surgical intervention system is described. The method consists of determining the articulation of a surgical intervention system with respect to a predetermined articulation of a virtual device. One or more parameters of the virtual device are mapped to a predetermined articulation of a surgical intervention system. The user may use a tool to identify the articulation of a surgical intervention system by referring to a predetermined articulation of a virtual device and adjusting the rotational forces
baseline_run1: A system and method for robot-assisted orthopedic surgery provides substantially stable, subspace-decomposed haptic guidance during bone resection for femoral acetabular impingement. Patient-specific three-dimensional models of the proximal femur and acetabulum are generated and used to define dynamic movement limits and target resection volumes for a robotic cutting tool. A haptic controller identifies first and second subsets of haptic interaction geometric primitives corresponding respectively to constraint-enforcing boundaries and desired cutting regions, and computes haptic forces in distinct subspaces to simultaneously enforce safety constraints and guide the surgeon toward the planned resection. The robotic system applies these subspace-based haptic forces to maintain tool motion within the dynamic limits while enabling smooth, stable, and accurate execution of the planned bone removal.
baseline_run2: A system for robot-assisted orthopedic surgery provides substantially stable haptic guidance during bone resection procedures. Patient-specific three-dimensional models of a joint are generated and used to define a first subset of haptic interaction geometric primitives corresponding to safe cutting regions and a second subset corresponding to motion-limiting boundaries. A computer determines haptic forces in a first subspace to guide a virtual or physical cutting tool along desired resection paths and determines haptic forces in a second, different subspace to constrain the tool within dynamic movement limits. The robotic system removes bone while the haptic feedback and subspace constraints inhibit tool motion outside of preplanned anatomical and surgical boundaries.
baseline_run3: A system and method for robot-assisted orthopedic surgery combine subspace-based haptic rendering with dynamically constrained tool guidance. Patient-specific three-dimensional models of a joint are generated and used to define geometric primitives that partition the haptic interaction space into at least a first subspace associated with safe cutting zones and a second subspace associated with restricted or no-cut regions. A robotic surgical tool is controlled to compute and apply haptic forces in the first and second subspaces, providing substantially stable feedback that guides the surgeon and resists motion into the restricted regions. Dynamic movement limits of the tool are updated in real time based on the subspace-specific haptic calculations and intraoperative data to ensure accurate bone removal while preventing violation of preplanned surgical boundaries.

ours_text: A surgical imaging system of the present invention includes a method for manipulating an image generated by a surgical instrument to provide a user with a guide to a surgical procedure. A computer-aided image processing tool detects the position of a surgical instrument at a focal point and transmits the image to the surgical instrument. The data generated by the surgical instrument are correlated with the image generated by the surgical instrument. During the operation, an end-to-end visual representation of the image is provided, and multiple images of the image are displayed in three-dimensional space.
baseline_run1: A system and method are provided for real-time intra-operative Q3D visualization and instrument guidance that integrates multi-camera IR-based 3D imaging with endoscopic Q3D modeling and tracking. An anatomical object is scanned and simultaneously imaged by multiple IR cameras and at least one Q3D endoscope, wherein parallax-derived integrated IR images are registered with Q3D endoscopic data to generate a unified intra-operative 3D model. Surgical instruments are tracked within this unified model, and virtual fields of view corresponding to instrument tips are generated to display predicted instrument paths and dynamically updated no-fly zones around critical anatomical structures. The system enables continuous, real-time, multi-perspective visualization and collision-avoidance guidance for instruments during minimally invasive procedures.
baseline_run2: A system and method are provided for real-time intra-operative 3D guidance that integrates Q3D endoscopic imaging with parallax-based IR multi-camera scanning. An anatomical object and surrounding instruments are imaged concurrently by a Q3D endoscope and a plurality of IR cameras mounted on or around surgical instruments. A processor fuses the Q3D scene model with the integrated IR-based 3D image to generate an enhanced, registered intra-operative 3D representation, identifies instruments and anatomical structures, and computes instrument trajectories with dynamic no-fly zones. The system further renders virtual fields of view from selected instrument perspectives to provide predictive path visualization and 3D tracking during surgical procedures.
baseline_run3: A system and method are provided for real-time intra-operative Q3D visualization and navigation that integrates multi-modal imaging with predictive instrument guidance. An anatomical region is scanned and concurrently imaged with a plurality of IR and optical cameras mounted on or around multiple surgical instruments to generate parallax-based integrated 3D and Q3D scene models. A processor fuses the scanner data, IR images, and optical images to produce a dynamically updated Q3D representation of target structures and instruments, and displays the scene from a selectable virtual instrument field of view. The processor further determines and visualizes no-fly zones around critical anatomy, predicts safe instrument paths within the Q3D model, and provides continuous 3D tracking and collision-avoidance feedback during intervention.

ours_text: 1 An operating room surgical tool system comprises a camera with a viewfinder, a camera with a viewfinder, a camera with a viewfinder, a camera with a viewfinder, a camera with a viewfinder, a camera with a viewfinder, a camera with a viewfinder, a camera with a viewfinder, a camera with a viewfinder, a camera with a viewfinder, and a camera with a viewfinder. 2 An end-axis position is performed to identify the position of a rotating instrument.
baseline_run1: A system and method for intraoperative three-dimensional imaging and measurement within a body cavity are disclosed. The system comprises multiple trocars with retractable, tracked cameras and at least one laparoscopic instrument incorporating a wide-field optical imaging module with an optional path folding mirror, and a primary high-resolution camera. An image processing unit receives images from the retractable cameras, the wide-field camera, and the primary camera, applies geometric and optical transforms based on tracked positional marks and known optical paths, and fuses the images to generate real-time stereoscopic and three-dimensional reconstructions of the surgical field. The reconstructed images are presented on a three-dimensional display to provide highly accurate depth perception and quantitative shape measurements for surgical guidance.
baseline_run2: A surgical imaging and assistance system for minimally invasive procedures comprising multiple instrument-mounted retractable cameras with fixed-reference tracking markers, at least one wide-field camera, and a laparoscope, all oriented toward a surgical target region. An optical tracking sensor determines the three-dimensional positions and orientations of the tracking markers, and an image processor receives images from the instrument-mounted cameras, the wide-field camera, and the laparoscope. The processor applies geometric and optical image transforms, including path-folding corrections for the wide-field camera, to co-register and fuse the images into a unified stereoscopic three-dimensional representation of the target and surrounding anatomy. The fused three-dimensional image is displayed on a stereoscopic monitor to enable accurate intra-abdominal shape measurement, depth perception, and tool guidance during surgery.
baseline_run3: A surgical visualization and navigation system is provided that combines trocar-mounted retractable cameras with a wide-field optical imaging subsystem to generate enhanced stereoscopic three-dimensional images of an internal surgical target. The system includes multiple instrument trocars each having integrated cameras with fixed positional relationships to optical tracking markers, at least one wide-field camera with optional path-folding mirrors, and a processor configured to receive images from both trocar and wide-field cameras. The processor tracks the positions of the markers to estimate camera geometries, applies image transforms to register and align the trocar and wide-field images, and fuses the transformed images into a stereoscopic three-dimensional representation of the operative field. The resulting stereoscopic image is displayed on a three-dimensional monitor to provide accurate depth perception and real-time measurement of anatomical structures during minimally invasive procedures.

ours_text: One method relates to a surgical imaging system comprising a manipulating device, an endoscope, and a camera. The manipulating device generates an image of the anatomical position of a patient in a surgical procedure. The imaging system is augmented to provide a virtual image of the anatomical position of a patient in a surgical procedure. In addition, the image is analyzed for accuracy by a data acquisition process. The data acquisition process may be performed remotely from the imaging system, including the acquisition of three-dimensional images of the anatomical position of objects.
baseline_run1: A system and method for intra-operative 3D imaging and motion-compensated navigation of moving anatomical targets combines tracked endoscopy with multi-camera IR-based surface reconstruction. An endoscope including a tracking mechanism records its position and orientation relative to target tissue while a motion sensor characterizes cyclical organ motion. Simultaneously, a plurality of IR cameras, mounted on surgical instruments or the operating environment, capture IR images that are integrated via parallax-based processing into a real-time 3D anatomical model registered to optical images. The correlated motion data and integrated 3D model enable dynamic updating of the target location and tool guidance to compensate for organ motion during medical procedures.
baseline_run2: A system and method for intra-operative guidance integrates endoscopic motion tracking with multi-camera infrared-based 3D imaging of anatomical structures. An endoscope equipped with a tracking mechanism records its positions and orientations relative to moving target tissue while a motion sensor characterizes cyclical organ motion. Simultaneously, multiple IR cameras, optionally mounted on surgical instruments, capture IR images that are fused via parallax to create a real-time 3D representation of the anatomical region. The recorded endoscope poses and organ motion data are correlated with the integrated 3D IR image to provide motion-compensated visualization and navigation during medical procedures.
baseline_run3: A system and method for real-time intra-operative imaging of moving target tissue combines tracked endoscopy with multi-camera infrared parallax imaging. An endoscope equipped with a position/orientation tracking mechanism is used in conjunction with multiple IR cameras mounted on surgical instruments or the operating room environment to capture reflected IR light from an anatomical region. The tracked endoscope positions and orientations are temporally correlated with cyclical organ motion data and integrated with the IR parallax images to generate a continuously updated 3D representation of the target tissue. The resulting intra-operative 3D image compensates for organ motion and provides enhanced spatial context for guidance of diagnostic or therapeutic procedures.

ours_text: A surgical instrument system comprises a robotic tool for manipulating a surgically performed joint and a guide device for adjusting the position of the surgically performed joint relative to the patient's body. The method includes a method of generating force to be applied to the surgically performed joint. The method includes a plurality of end-pieces, including a first-axis receptacle and a cutting device. The receptacle is positioned in a pre-determined position relative to the patient's body, and the cutting device is positioned in.
baseline_run1: A system and method for robot-assisted orthopedic implant extraction are provided. A robotic arm having an end effector is configured to manipulate an implant extractor tool having pivotably connected jaws and a one-hand operable adjustment mechanism. A robotic controller monitors the position and orientation of the end effector and the extractor jaws, and applies controlled forces to an implant while tracking bone motion via one or more trackers affixed to the bone. The controller determines soft tissue balance and extraction force parameters in real time and outputs guidance and/or automatically adjusts the extractor tool to achieve safe, balanced implant removal.
baseline_run2: A system and method for robot-assisted implant extraction are disclosed. The system includes a robotic arm having an end effector coupled to an implant extraction tool with pivotably connected jaws and a one-hand operable adjustment mechanism. A robotic controller monitors the position and orientation of the end effector and applies controlled forces to the implant and associated bone structures based on tracking data from one or more trackers affixed to the bone. The controller determines soft tissue balance during implant engagement and extraction and dynamically adjusts the extraction tool and robotic arm motion to optimize implant removal while minimizing soft tissue disruption.
baseline_run3: A system and method are provided for robot-assisted extraction of orthopedic implants. A robotic arm having an end effector is configured to couple to a one-handed implant extractor tool including pivotably connected arms, jaws for engaging an implant, and an adjustment mechanism controlled by an actuator. A robotic controller monitors position and orientation of the end effector and extractor tool via a tracking system, and applies controlled forces to the implant and surrounding bone based on soft tissue balance data derived from tracker information. The controller dynamically adjusts the extractor’s engagement and biasing forces to optimize implant removal while maintaining desired soft tissue balance, and outputs corresponding metrics to a display.

ours_text: A method is provided for manipulating a portion of a limb to determine the position of a joint relative to the first and second vertebral bones of the limb. The method includes a force sensor and a reversible alignment device. The force sensor is positioned at the proximal end of the limb, and the reversible alignment device is positioned at the distal end of the limb. The reversible alignment device is covered by a flexible plastic covering system comprising a plurality of movable structures, including a bone.
baseline_run1: A system and method are provided for robot-assisted ligament balancing during orthopedic surgery. The system includes a robotic arm having an end effector configured to engage a tensor/ligament balancer comprising first and second paddles and a biasing member operable to apply a substantially constant force to the second paddle to measure a joint gap. A robotic controller monitors the position and orientation of the end effector and the paddles, receives tracking information from one or more trackers affixed to patient anatomy, and determines soft tissue balance based on the measured gap under controlled force conditions. The calculated soft tissue balance and corresponding gap measurements are output to a display and can be used to automatically or semi-automatically adjust the position of the end effector to achieve a desired ligament tension profile.
baseline_run2: A system and method for robot-assisted soft tissue balancing is provided. The system includes a robotic arm having an end effector operably coupled to a tensor/ligament balancer comprising first and second paddles and a biasing member configured to apply a substantially constant force between opposing anatomical structures. A robotic controller monitors the position and orientation of the end effector and paddles, and determines a real-time soft tissue balance metric based on the gap measured by the balancer and tracking data from markers affixed to the bone. The soft tissue balance information is used to guide robotic manipulation of the joint and can be output to a display to assist in surgical planning and execution.
baseline_run3: A system and method for robot-assisted soft tissue balancing during joint arthroplasty is disclosed. The system includes a robotic arm having an end effector configured to operably couple to a tensor/ligament balancer comprising first and second paddles and a biasing member applying a substantially constant force between opposing bony structures. A controller monitors position and orientation of the end effector and the paddles via a tracking system and determines joint gap dimensions and soft tissue balance under controlled, repeatable loading conditions. The determined balance metrics are used to guide robotic adjustment of bone preparation and/or implant positioning, and are output to a display for intraoperative decision-making.

ours_text: A method comprises a computer-aided robotic system for detecting and mapping the position of a patient during a surgical procedure. The system generates an image of a device based on the information provided by one or more sensors in the system. The system generates an image of a device based on the information provided by one or more sensors in the system. In addition, the system may be configured to display the orientation and orientation of a reference scene from a physical location to a three-dimensional perspective, and to display the orientation and orientation of a reference scene from a virtual location
baseline_run1: A system and method for preventing unintended tool motion in robotic-assisted ophthalmic surgery. The system comprises a robotic surgical instrument with integrated inertial sensors and kinematic tracking, an imaging assembly configured to generate a three-dimensional model of a patient’s eye and establish a global coordinate system, and a processor coupled to receive movement and imaging data. The processor is configured to identify unintentional movements of the surgical instrument within the global coordinate system and, in response, generate control signals to suppress, filter, or constrain such movements relative to a predefined virtual boundary. In some embodiments, the system dynamically updates the virtual boundary based on real-time eye motion and tool position to further reduce the risk of inadvertent injury.
baseline_run2: A system and method are provided for robotic-assisted surgical control incorporating unintentional motion detection. A robotic surgery platform establishes a global coordinate system for a target anatomy using kinematic data and volumetric imaging to generate a registered three-dimensional model and define virtual safety boundaries. One or more freely moveable surgeon controllers equipped with inertial sensors provide movement data used to command robotic instruments within the coordinate system. A processor analyzes the movement data to identify unintentional movements of the controllers and, based on this identification and the virtual boundaries, selectively filters, attenuates, or blocks corresponding robotic motions to reduce the risk of inadvertent tissue injury.
baseline_run3: A system and method for intention-aware robotic-assisted microsurgery are disclosed. The system includes a surgical robotic manipulator and handheld controller equipped with inertial sensors, optical coherence tomography imaging, and kinematic tracking to establish a unified global coordinate system of the surgical field. A processor analyzes movement data from the controller and robotic joints to distinguish intentional tool motions from unintentional movements, and dynamically enforces virtual safety boundaries within the registered three-dimensional model of the patient’s anatomy. Upon detecting unintentional movement, the system selectively filters, attenuates, or overrides corresponding robot commands to prevent tool motion beyond defined safety zones and reduce risk of inadvertent injury.

ours_text: A surgical apparatus comprises a surgical tool system for generating an image of a surgical instrument and a surgical tool system for manipulating a surgical instrument. The surgical tool system includes a method for determining the relative position of a surgical instrument and a surgical tool system. In addition, the method may be configured to allow a user to rotate the surgical instrument from one end to the other. The method may be configured to allow a user to remove a portion of the surgical instrument from the surgical tool system by means of a first-axis rotation and a third-axis rotation.
baseline_run1: A robotic-assisted surgical system is provided that integrates a globally registered coordinate framework with a multi-blade, torque-transferring retractor assembly for ophthalmic or microsurgical procedures. The system includes an overhead imaging assembly and tool-based sensors that generate a computer-registered three-dimensional model of the patient’s eye and surrounding anatomy, and define virtual boundaries within the coordinate system. A retractor instrument having first and second blades rotatably coupled to a clevis and linked via a torque-transferring tension member is tracked and controlled within this coordinate system so that blade orientation and opening are robotically actuated while respecting the virtual boundaries.
